anhydrous_ethanol_min_purity.label: STANDARD
anhydrous_ethanol_min_purity.note: Applies to the neat anhydrous ethanol delivered by the distillery, before blending. IS 15464 was revised in 2022; the 2022 text was not retrieved for this project, so check whether the revision adds an explicit Karl Fischer water row.

absolute_alcohol_max_water.unit: % v/v water in ethyl alcohol, maximum
absolute_alcohol_max_water.source: is15464_2004, clause 3.2 (definition of Ethyl Alcohol / Absolute Alcohol)
absolute_alcohol_max_water.label: STANDARD
absolute_alcohol_max_water.note: This is where the original repo's "0.5 % / 5,000 ppm" comes from. It is a limit on water in NEAT ethanol (a definition), not the water tolerance of the E20 blend. 0.5 % v/v is also not exactly 5,000 ppm by mass.

e20_max_water_content.unit: % v/v water in E20 fuel, maximum
e20_max_water_content.source: is17943_2022, Table 1, Sl No. (xix) (test method ISO 12937, Karl Fischer)
e20_max_water_content.label: STANDARD
e20_max_water_content.note: IS 17943:2022 is the E20 REFERENCE fuel (type-approval / COP testing). The retail E20 specification is IS 17021:2018, which was not retrieved; IS 17943's foreword says it is derived from IS 17021 with closer tolerances. Treat this as the best available sourced quality limit. It is a quality limit, far below the phase-separation point.

e20_max_phase_separation_temperature.unit: °C, maximum (blend must stay single-phase down to this temperature)
e20_max_phase_separation_temperature.source: is17943_2022, Table 1, Sl No. (xii), Annex B
e20_max_phase_separation_temperature.label: STANDARD

e10_max_ethanol_content.label: STANDARD
e10_max_ethanol_content.note: The Raman dataset's samples are European (DE) gasolines, E0–E10.

correlation.form: W_tol [wt %] = a*T^2 + b*T + c,  T in °C,  E = ethanol % v/v
correlation.unit: wt % water in the total blend
correlation.source: coleman2012_us8268629, col. 10, lines 36-50; the patent cites french2005 for the underlying phase-equilibrium data
correlation.label: LITERATURE VALUE
correlation.note: The patent does not state the fitted range of ethanol content or temperature. Cross-checks: (1) at E10, 15.6 °C it gives 0.63 wt %, about 0.47 % v/v, consistent with 0.5 % v/v at 60 °F in korotney1995 Fig. 1; (2) at 25 % v/v ethanol, 0 °C it gives 1.93 wt % vs 1.78-1.88 % mass measured by haq1990 (p. 352-353). Real tolerance also depends on aromatics and other oxygenates (gramajo2004), which this correlation ignores.

e10_check_point.unit: % v/v water tolerated by E10 at 60 °F (15.6 °C)
e10_check_point.label: LITERATURE VALUE

haq_e25_0c_check_point.unit: % mass water tolerated by 25/75 v/v ethanol/gasoline at 0 °C
haq_e25_0c_check_point.label: LITERATURE VALUE

ethanol_mass_fraction.unit: kg ethanol per kg of separated lower (aqueous) phase
ethanol_mass_fraction.label: ASSUMPTION
ethanol_mass_fraction.note: Simplification: once separation starts, the lower phase is treated as a fixed-composition ethanol-water mixture. korotney1995 (p. 3) and grains2026 state qualitatively that the lower phase is ethanol-rich; a real model needs ternary tie-line data (french2005). Used only to estimate the lower-phase VOLUME shown on the site, not the separation onset.

density_ethanol.unit: kg/m3 (upper bound from relative density 0.7961 at 15.6/15.6 °C)
density_ethanol.label: STANDARD

density_gasoline.label: STANDARD
density_gasoline.note: Used only to convert the Johansen & Schramm mass fractions to % v/v; the published blends' exact density is not reported.

density_e20.source: is17943_2022, Table 1, Sl No. (i) — midpoint of 743-760
density_e20.label: STANDARD

capacity_m3.label: ASSUMPTION
capacity_m3.note: Typical retail UST size in India is reported as 15-20 kL; confirm with OMC drawings.

delivery_trigger_fraction.label: ASSUMPTION
delivery_trigger_fraction.note: Reorder when fill drops below this fraction.

ullage_ambient_coupling.label: ASSUMPTION
ullage_ambient_coupling.note: Ullage gas temperature = ground temperature + coupling x (ambient - ground). Buried tanks are damped by soil; the vent/fill pipes couple the vapour space to the air. Needs measured ullage temperatures.

fuel_temperature_source.label: ASSUMPTION
fuel_temperature_source.note: Bulk fuel temperature is taken as the ERA5 28-100 cm soil temperature (proxy for a buried tank).

moisture_capture_efficiency.label: ASSUMPTION
moisture_capture_efficiency.note: Fraction of water vapour in inhaled air that ends up in the fuel. 1.0 is an upper bound (fuel far from saturation acts as a desiccant).

seal_fault_catchment_m2.unit: m2 of rainfall catchment draining into the tank through a faulty fill/manhole seal
seal_fault_catchment_m2.label: ASSUMPTION
seal_fault_catchment_m2.note: 'major' represents a flooded spill box / manhole draining through a damaged fill cap.

wet_tanker_water_L.unit: L free water per wet delivery
wet_tanker_water_L.label: ASSUMPTION

wet_tanker_probability.unit: probability a given delivery carries residual water
wet_tanker_probability.label: ASSUMPTION

delivered_fuel_water_source.source: is17943_2022, Table 1, Sl No. (xix) — worst-case compliant delivery
delivered_fuel_water_source.label: STANDARD
delivered_fuel_water_source.note: Each delivered load enters at the E20 water limit (0.050 % v/v, about 0.066 wt %).

free_water_redissolves.label: ASSUMPTION
free_water_redissolves.note: A settled lower phase is not re-mixed when the fuel warms (no agitation in a UST).

bottom_water_dissolution_kg_per_day.unit: kg/day of settled bottom water dissolving into the fuel when the fuel is dry (scales with 1 - saturation)
bottom_water_dissolution_kg_per_day.label: ASSUMPTION
bottom_water_dissolution_kg_per_day.note: Liquid water entering the tank settles to the bottom (denser than fuel) and dissolves through the interface at a finite rate. Vapour taken up by breathing goes straight into solution. A real value needs interface mass-transfer measurements; it controls how much a drain-out can remove before the water dissolves.

water_sensor_sigma_mg_per_kg.unit: mg/kg (1 sigma) for the periodic dissolved-water test of the tank contents
water_sensor_sigma_mg_per_kg.label: ASSUMPTION
water_sensor_sigma_mg_per_kg.note: Represents a daily sample test (Karl Fischer or an in-tank sensor). Layer A's Raman water model is NOT validated at near-saturation water levels.

free_phase_dispensed.label: ASSUMPTION
free_phase_dispensed.note: The submersible pump suction sits above the bottom; only dissolved water leaves with dispensed fuel.

tank_diameter_m.label: ASSUMPTION
tank_diameter_m.note: Horizontal cylinder; used to convert bottom-phase volume to gauge height.

margin_definition.value: 1 - (dissolved + settled bottom + lower-phase water) / tolerance(T_fuel, ethanol); <= 0 exactly when a lower phase exists (clamped to 0 if dilution alone would make it positive)
margin_definition.label: DESIGN CHOICE

act_horizon_h.source: DESIGN CHOICE (matches the 24-48 h lead-time goal in the proposal)
act_horizon_h.label: DESIGN CHOICE

watch_margin.label: DESIGN CHOICE
watch_margin.note: WATCH if forecast margin falls below this within watch_horizon_h.

alert_quantile.label: DESIGN CHOICE
alert_quantile.note: The GBM alert uses its 10th-percentile margin forecast (conservative), the point forecast is used for MAE.

act_margin.label: DESIGN CHOICE
act_margin.note: ACT if forecast margin reaches 0 (separation) within act_horizon_h.

method.value: PI = t(0.975, df) * RMSECV * sqrt(1 + h_new); PASS if whole PI inside limits, FAIL if whole PI outside, else REVIEW
method.label: LITERATURE VALUE
